topIssues.title: op-challenger run-trace dispatches super-cannon-kona to single-chain Kona executor
topIssues.author: wwared
topIssues.body:
## Summary

`op-challenger run-trace` cannot exercise the `super-cannon-kona` game type. The runner's trace-provider factory dispatches both `CannonKonaGameType` and `SuperCannonKonaGameType` through the single-chain `vm.NewKonaExecutor()`, while the production challenger registers `SuperCannonKonaGameType` against `vm.NewKonaSuperExecutor()`. The two executors invoke different Kona-host CLI subcommands (`single` vs `super`) with disjoint flag sets and disjoint input shapes, so a `super-cannon-kona` run-trace invocation produces a Kona-host command that does not run super-state derivation at all.

## Routing divergence

`op-challenger/runner/factory.go:41-49` — runner factory (used by `run-trace`):

```go
case gameTypes.CannonKonaGameType, gameTypes.SuperCannonKonaGameType:
    serverExecutor := vm.NewKonaExecutor()
    stateConverter := cannon.NewStateConverter(cfg.CannonKona)
    prestate, err := prestateSource.getPrestate(ctx, logger, cfg.CannonKonaAbsolutePreStateBaseURL, cfg.CannonKonaAbsolutePreState, dir, stateConverter)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    prestateProvider := vm.NewPrestateProvider(prestate, stateConverter)
    return cannon.NewTraceProvider(logger, m, cfg.CannonKona, serverExecutor, prestateProvider, prestate, localInputs, dir, 42), nil
```

`op-challenger/game/fault/register.go:77-83` — production challenger registry:

```go
if cfg.GameTypeEnabled(gameTypes.SuperCannonKonaGameType) {
    rootProvider, superNodeProvider, syncValidator, err := clients.SuperchainClients()
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    registerTasks = append(registerTasks, NewSuperCannonKonaRegisterTask(gameTypes.SuperCannonKonaGameType, cfg, m, vm.NewKonaSuperExecutor(), rootProvider, superNodeProvider, syncValidator))
}
```

The registry uses `KonaSuperExecutor`; the runner factory uses `KonaExecutor` for the same game type. Only one of the two paths is correct for super-cannon-kona.

## Subcommand and flag divergence

`KonaExecutor` (`op-challenger/game/fault/trace/vm/kona_server_executor.go:25-69`) emits the Kona-host `single` subcommand, requires exactly one entry in `cfg.L2s` (errors at line 26-28 otherwise), reads `inputs.L2Head` / `inputs.L2OutputRoot` (lines 36-37), and ignores `inputs.AgreedPreState`.

`KonaSuperExecutor` (`op-challenger/game/fault/trace/vm/kona_super_server_executor.go:25-65`) emits the Kona-host `super` subcommand, accepts a CSV `--l2-node-addresses` (line 35), reads `inputs.AgreedPreState` (line 37) and `inputs.L2Claim` as `--claimed-l2-post-state` (line 38), and supports `--depset-cfg` (line 58).

These are different code paths inside Kona — `bin/host/src/cli/single.rs` vs `bin/host/src/cli/super.rs` — with different derivation and validation logic.

## Input-shape divergence

`createGameInputsInterop` (`op-challenger/runner/game_inputs.go:167-231`), the runner's input builder for `SuperCannonKonaGameType`, populates `AgreedPreState` (line 226) and a synthetic `L2SequenceNumber` (line 228) but does **not** populate `L2Head` or `L2OutputRoot`; both remain zero.

When the resulting `LocalGameInputs` flows through `KonaExecutor` via the runner factory's wrong branch, `KonaExecutor.OracleCommand` reads zero hashes for `--agreed-l2-head-hash` and `--agreed-l2-output-root` (`kona_server_executor.go:36-37`) and ignores the populated `AgreedPreState`. The resulting Kona-host command runs single-chain derivation against zero hashes plus a super-state hash assigned to `--claimed-l2-output-root`. This produces either an immediate error or a derivation that returns an invalid status root — not the super-state re-derivation the runner intends.

## Consequence

`op-challenger run-trace --run super-cannon-kona/<name>[/<prestate>]` cannot succeed against a real super-state input on any chain. The runner will repeatedly invoke a Kona-host command that has no path to a successful output-root verification for super-cannon-kona.

This is silent: the runner does not detect the routing mismatch, the Kona-host invocation fails for what looks like a derivation-level reason, and the runner records the failure under `RecordVmFailure` with a reason that does not surface the real cause.

## Test coverage

No test in `op-challenger/`, `op-acceptance-tests/`, `op-e2e/`, or `op-devstack/` invokes `op-challenger run-trace --run super-cannon-kona/...`. `op-challenger/cmd/run_trace_test.go` covers only single `cannon` / `cannon-kona`. `op-challenger/runner/runner_test.go` is a stubbed timeout test. `KonaSuperExecutor` is unit-tested directly in `kona_super_server_executor_test.go` but never reached through the run-trace entry point.

## Suggested fix shape

`op-challenger/runner/factory.go` should split the `CannonKonaGameType` and `SuperCannonKonaGameType` cases. The super-cannon-kona branch needs:

- `vm.NewKonaSuperExecutor()` instead of `vm.NewKonaExecutor()`.
- A trace-provider constructor that accepts the super-state input shape produced by `createGameInputsInterop`, mirroring how `register.go`'s `NewSuperCannonKonaRegisterTask` wires the production challenger.
- Correct propagation of dependency-set config so `--depset-cfg` is set when present.

A runner-level test that constructs a `super-cannon-kona` `RunConfig` and asserts the resulting Kona-host command starts with `super` and includes `--agreed-l2-pre-state`, `--claimed-l2-post-state`, and `--l2-node-addresses` would prevent regression.

topPRs.title: test(op-acceptance): drive AfterChainHead test setup via TestSequencer
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Adds the 6 AfterChainHead subtests to the SuperFaultProofs acceptance suite and converts the existing tests' Stage 1+2 setup to deterministic block production via `TestSequencer` (replacing the running-sequencer flow). Drops `MarkFlaky` on the two varied-block-time tests — the original flake (`ethereum-optimism/optimism#19828`) is no longer reachable now that `nextTimestampAfterSafeHeads` walks past no-op transitions and `TestSequencer` drives every chain to the boundary deterministically.

Two new subtests (`DisputeTimestampAfterChainHeadConsolidate`, `DisputeBlockAfterChainHead-FirstChain`) skip their challenger halves under varied-block-time configs pending op-supernode bug `ethereum-optimism/optimism#20481` (`VerifiedRequiredL1` uses MIN of per-chain L1s instead of MAX). Their FPP halves still run.

Also bumps `GossipTimestampThreshold` to 1h in the devstack p2p config — devstack chain timestamps are synthetic and can lag wallclock during long tests, so the production-default 60s "payload too old" check rejects otherwise-valid TestSequencer-produced blocks. Devstack-only.

## Test plan

- [x] `TestInteropFaultProofs` — PASS (97s) locally
- [x] `TestInteropFaultProofs_VariedBlockTimes` — PASS (100s) locally
- [x] `TestInteropFaultProofs_VariedBlockTimes_FasterChainB` — PASS (100s) locally

topPRs.title: op-supernode: avoid engine rewind on L1 reorg
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- Stop resetting chain engines for pure `DecisionRewind` handling caused by L1 reorgs.
- Keep the rewind scoped to Supernode-owned state when no invalidation is being undone: `VerifiedDB`, deny-list pruning, and `LogsDB`.
- If the rewind would prune any deny-list entry, persist `ResetAllChainsTo = lastTS - 1` in the rewind plan and reset all chain engines after the DB cleanup succeeds.

## Motivation

`DecisionRewind` means previously accepted Supernode state no longer lines up with canonical L1. That can happen when L1 reorg handling invalidates previously accepted cross-chain verification state, and it does not necessarily mean any chain engine executed an invalid block.

Previously, the rewind plan populated `ResetAllChainsTo` whenever there was a previous verified timestamp. During apply, every chain engine was reset before the logs DB rewind/clear completed. For a pure L1 reorg, this is more disruptive than the state correction requires: the virtual nodes can be stopped, engines receive synthetic/target forkchoice updates, derivation may need to restart from the reset point, and the backend can look unhealthy while the engine is being reset. Those engine-side effects are unnecessary when only Supernode acceptance state needs to move back to match canonical L1.

The exception is deny-list cleanup. If an L1 reorg rewind prunes a deny-list entry, the prior invalidation may have already moved an engine onto a replacement/deposits-only path. Once that deny-list entry is removed, the engines need a chance to re-derive without that stale invalidation. Deny-list entries are expected to be rare, so this PR chooses the simpler conservative behavior: if any chain has a deny-list entry that will be pruned, reset all chain engines to `lastTS - 1`.

## Crash-safety / ordering

The reset decision is captured in the persisted rewind plan before any side effects are applied. That matters because applying the rewind prunes deny-list entries; if the node crashes after pruning but before engine reset, replaying the WAL still needs to know that engine repair is required.

Engine resets now run after `VerifiedDB`, deny-list, and `LogsDB` cleanup succeed. If the local DB cleanup fails, the pending transition remains and we avoid repeatedly resetting engines before the state rewind has completed.

## Testing

- `go test ./op-supernode/supernode/activity/interop`
- `go test ./op-supernode/supernode/chain_container`
- `go test ./op-supernode/supernode/...`

topPRs.title: feat(op-reth): convert built payload to execution data
topPRs.author: mattsse
topPRs.body:
Adds an `OpBuiltPayload::into_execution_data` conversion that builds `OpExecutionData` from the sealed block, plus `From<OpBuiltPayload>` impls for both `OpExecutionData` and the local `OpExecData` wrapper. This gives op-reth the same infallible built-payload-to-execution-data path as upstream reth and prepares for the upcoming payload trait bound change.

See also paradigmxyz/reth#23859.
